summary: Specifies a data model for managing Sieve email filtering scripts on a server using JMAP. Clients can efficiently search, access, organize and validate scripts through this protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: Sieve scripts are rules that sort your email automatically. This lets an email app look at, edit and check those rules on the server using a modern web-style language.

questions: how to manage sieve scripts with jmap
what is the jmap sieve capability
how to activate a sieve script over jmap
subtitle: How a JMAP client lists, uploads, activates and validates email-filtering Sieve scripts on a server.

tldr.problem: Email filter rules written in Sieve live on the server, but managing them has relied on ManageSieve. JMAP clients had no consistent way to handle them.
tldr.mechanism: It defines a SieveScript data type with get, set, query and validate methods. Script text is uploaded as a blob, and at most one script per user is active.
tldr.outcome: A server can offer the same scripts over JMAP and ManageSieve. Servers that implement the JMAP VacationResponse as a Sieve script have extra rules to follow.

today: RFC 9661 is a Proposed Standard from September 2024. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Sieve Scripts over JMAP
sections.content:
RFC 9661 defines a data model for managing Sieve scripts (RFC 5228) on a server using the JSON Meta Application Protocol, JMAP (RFC 8620). The model is designed so a server can give consistent access to the same scripts through ManageSieve (RFC 5804) and JMAP.

A Sieve script filters email messages at the time of final delivery. Servers MUST support all properties the RFC defines for the SieveScript data type.
sections.plainLanguage: Sieve is a list of rules for your mail, like putting letters from school in one tray. This lets a modern app edit that list on the server.

sections.title: The Sieve Capability
sections.content:
Support is announced with the capability URI urn:ietf:params:jmap:sieve. The session-level value carries an implementation string with the name and version of the Sieve implementation.

Each account also reports its limits:

  • maxSizeScriptName: at least 512 octets, for ManageSieve compatibility.
  • maxSizeScript and maxNumberScripts: largest script and most scripts, or null for no limit.
  • maxNumberRedirects: most redirect actions in a single evaluation, or null.
  • sieveExtensions: the supported Sieve extensions.
  • notificationMethods and externalLists: supported URI schemes for the enotify and extlists extensions, or null.
sections.plainLanguage: The server tells the app how many rules it allows, how big they can be and which special tricks it knows.

sections.title: The SieveScript Object
sections.content:
A SieveScript has four properties:

  • id: immutable, set by the server.
  • name: a string or null. If set, it must be a Net-Unicode string of at least 1 character and unique within the account. Servers MUST reject names containing certain control characters, and MAY reject names that break server policy, such as names containing a slash.
  • blobId: the blob holding the script's raw octets.
  • isActive: whether the script is currently filtering incoming messages. It defaults to false.

A user may have at most one active script. Script content MUST be UTF-8 of at least 1 character, valid Sieve, and MUST NOT require capability strings the server does not list. It is uploaded and downloaded as a blob through the JMAP upload and download URLs or the Blob management methods of RFC 9404.
sections.plainLanguage: Each rule list has a name, a place where its text is kept, and an on/off flag. Only one list can be switched on at a time.

sections.title: Methods: get, set, query, validate
sections.content:
SieveScript/get is a standard get, and its ids argument may be null to fetch all scripts. It matches the ManageSieve LISTSCRIPTS command, and downloading content matches GETSCRIPT.

SieveScript/set is a standard set with two extra arguments. onSuccessActivateScript names a script to activate, and onSuccessDeactivateScript set to true deactivates the current one. Both take effect only if all creations, updates and destructions succeed, and deactivation is processed first. The active script MUST NOT be destroyed unless deactivated in a separate set call.

Errors include alreadyExists (with existingId) for duplicate names, tooLarge above maxSizeScript, overQuota, invalidSieve for bad grammar or unsupported extensions, and sieveIsActive when destroying the active script.

SieveScript/query filters by name (contains the string) and isActive, and MUST support sorting by both. SieveScript/validate takes an account and a blob id and checks a script without storing it, returning an invalidSieve error or null. It matches CHECKSCRIPT.
sections.plainLanguage: You can list your rule lists, add, rename or delete them, search them, or test one before saving. Switching on a new list switches off the old one in the same step.

sections.title: Quotas and Vacation Responses
sections.content:
Servers SHOULD impose quotas on Sieve scripts so malicious users cannot exhaust storage. Quota administration is out of scope, but RFC 9425 defines a JMAP data model for quotas.

Some servers implement the JMAP VacationResponse from RFC 8621 as a Sieve script stored with the user's other scripts. Such servers MUST let it be fetched by SieveScript/get and activated or deactivated through onSuccessActivateScript. They MUST NOT let it be destroyed or have its content updated through SieveScript/set, and MUST reject such requests with a forbidden error.
sections.plainLanguage: The auto-reply rule shows up in your list and can be switched on or off there, but it has to be edited in its own special place.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
All security considerations of JMAP and Sieve apply. Implementations MUST treat script content as untrusted data. Parsers MUST fail gracefully on invalid or malicious content and be prepared for resource exhaustion, such as enormous strings, lists or command blocks.

IANA registered the urn:ietf:params:jmap:sieve capability, the SieveScript data type, and the error codes invalidSieve and sieveIsActive.
sections.plainLanguage: Treat a rule list from outside like a stranger's note: read it carefully and do not let a huge or tricky one break the mail system.
